title: Somnolence

rationale.Ca / PTH / PTHrP: High Ca, low PTH, elevated PTHrP = malignancy.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive somnolence, confusion, fatigue, constipation, polyuria, polydipsia, and nausea. Labs: elevated calcium (>11), low PTH (rules out primary hyperparathyroidism), elevated PTHrP. Hypercalcemia of malignancy is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in hospitalized patients. Mechanisms: PTHrP secretion (squamous cell cancers — lung, head/neck), osteolytic bone metastases (breast, multiple myeloma), excess 1,25-vitamin D (lymphoma). Treatment: aggressive IV normal saline (3-4L/day) to promote calciuresis. Then IV bisphosphonates (zoledronic acid or pamidronate — inhibit osteoclast activity). Calcitonin for rapid short-term reduction. Denosumab if refractory. Treat underlying malignancy. Monitor for arrhythmias (shortened QT on ECG).
